TI Determinants Factors of Stunting among Children Under Five in
   Timor-Leste: Evidence from Ermera, Viqueque, and Oe-Cusse
SO INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF SPECIAL EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE Stunting; maternal knowledge; family income; culture; infectious
   diseases; and exclusive breastfeeding
AB Stunting remains a serious public health problem in Timor-Leste, particularly among children under five years of age. This study aimed to analyze factors associated with stunting among children under five in the Ermera, Viqueque, and Oe-Cusse districts in 2025. This research used an analytic observational design with a cross-sectional approach. The study involved 421 children under five selected using multistage cluster sampling and systematic random sampling. Data were collected through structured interviews with mothers or caregivers using questionnaires and anthropometric measurements. Stunting status was determined based on height-for-age (HAZ) with a Z-score < -2 SD according to WHO standards. The dependent variable was stunting, while independent variables included infectious diseases, family income, maternal knowledge, culture, and exclusive breastfeeding. Data were analyzed using univariate and multivariate analyses with binary logistic regression at a significance level of p < 0.05. The results indicated that the prevalence of stunting among children under five years of age was 49.9%. Multivariate logistic regression analysis revealed that infectious diseases (p = 0.019; OR = 6.642), family income (p < 0.001; OR = 34.224), maternal knowledge (p = 0.001; OR = 19.796), culture (p = 0.018; OR = 6.269), and exclusive breastfeeding (p = 0.008; OR = 8.986) were significantly associated with stunting. Among these variables, family income was identified as the most dominant factor influencing stunting. In conclusion, stunting among children under five in the study areas is influenced by socioeconomic, health, behavioral, and cultural factors. Therefore, multisectoral interventions focusing on improving family economic conditions, maternal nutrition knowledge, infectious disease prevention, and promotion of exclusive breastfeeding are essential to reduce the prevalence of stunting in Timor-Leste.

Following a six-week SRSD-based intervention, students demonstrated statistically significant gains across all writing domains (p < .001, d = 1.04). Qualitative data indicated enhanced metacognitive awareness and confidence in managing academic discourse. These findings support the efficacy of structured, strategy-focused instruction in mitigating writing inequities in under-resourced ESL settings and affirm SRSD as a viable pedagogical model for fostering writer agency and academic literacy (Harris, 2022; Zhang & Hyland, 2023).

TI The Influence of Workplace Environment on Employee Burnout and Coping
   Mechanisms
SO INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF SPECIAL EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE Workplace environment; burnout; coping strategies; role clarity;
   workload; managerial support; employee well-being
ID IMPACT
AB Background: Employee burnout has also emerged as a major issue in all types of industries, especially the high-stress industries, which include healthcare, education, and finance. Workload, managerial support, and role clarity are some of the environmental factors in the workplace that contribute to burnout and the coping strategies of individuals. This paper examines how these environmental factors within the workplace affect employee burnout and establishes the coping mechanisms adopted by the workers to deal with stress in the Indian organisations. These relations are significant to understand and identify effective interventions to decrease burnout and enhance employee well-being. Methods: A convergent parallel mixed methods approach was used to gather both quantitative and qualitative data. The quantitative data were gathered through the application of three standardised measures, including the Revised Work Environment Scale (WES-R) , the Maslach Burnout Inventory-General Survey (MBI-GS), and the Brief Coping Orientation to Problems Experienced (COPE) inventory. The use of semi-structured interviews was aimed at getting qualitative data on what participants believed about their workplace, stressors, and coping strategies. The data were analysed using descriptive statistics, thematic analysis, hierarchical regression analysis, and Pearson correlation. Results: Workload was found to be the most significant predictor of burnout (b = 0.31, p < 0.001), with role clarity (b =-0.29, p < 0.001) and managerial support (b =-0.27, p < 0.001) being significant in reducing levels of burnout. Adaptive coping strategies like active coping (M = 4.3) and planning (M = 4.1) were commonly used and resulted in reduced burnout. Sector-specific differences in levels of burnout were found, with healthcare workers reporting the highest levels of burnout (M = 3.9), followed by education (M = 3.8) and finance (M = 3.7). Conclusion: This study emphasizes the importance of factors in the workplace environment and coping strategies in the mitigation of burnout. Interventions that focus on workload management and supporting managers may help to reduce burnout and improve employee well-being.

TI Vietnamese Law on Private Archives During the National Renewal Period
   (1986 - 2025)
SO INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF SPECIAL EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE private archival materials; private archives; people's archives;
   archival law; Vietnamese archives
AB This article presents the results of a study on the formation and development of Vietnamese law governing private archives and private archival materials during the national renewal (& Dstrok;oi moi) period from 1986 to 2025, situated within the broader context of changing state perceptions and the demands of international integration. In Vietnam, from the late twentieth century, private archives gradually emerged as a subject of scholarly attention; however, the early legal framework remained largely focused on records from the public sector. Legal instruments such as the 1982 Ordinance on the Protection of National Archival Materials and the 2001 Ordinance on Archives recognized private archives as an independent legal category, yet related regulations primarily emphasized registration, guidance, or protection of archival materials deemed to be of "special value" held by individuals, families, and lineages. A major turning point was marked by the 2011 Law on Archives, which for the first time formally acknowledged ownership rights and rights of disposition over private archival materials, while establishing mechanisms for registration, donation, and deposit in state archival institutions. This process of legal refinement was further consolidated in the 2024 Law on Archives (effective from 1 July 2025), which provides a clear definition of "private archives" and devotes an entire chapter to regulating this field. This new approach reflects a more open and objective legal mindset, expanding the regulatory scope from the public sector to include the private sector, thereby ensuring equality, respecting ownership rights, and encouraging the use and promotion of the value of private archival materials. Employing historical and logical methods alongside an interdisciplinary approach, the study elucidates the transformation in Vietnam's legal perception from viewing private archives merely as a supplementary element to recognizing them as an integral component of the national archival system. The current legal framework not only establishes safeguards and mechanisms for enhancing the value of private archival materials but also promotes scientific research, fosters international cooperation, and meets the requirements of integration in the new development stage.

TI Exploring Preservice Teachers' Attitudes toward Inclusive Education for
   Students with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD)
SO INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF SPECIAL EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE attitude scale; inclusive education; preservice teachers; students with
   autism
ID CHILDREN
AB The aim of this study is to examine preservice teachers' attitudes toward inclusive education for students with autism spectrum disorder (ASD). A total of 244 preservice teachers from various departments participated in this research. Data were gathered using a multi-dimensional attitude scale and analyzed through descriptive statistics, independent samples t-tests, and one-way ANOVA. The findings show that preservice teachers generally maintain a positive and supportive attitude toward ASD inclusion. Among the sub-dimensions, sensitivity received the highest scores, followed by education & training and professional self-efficacy. Statistical analysis indicated that, although gender did not significantly affect attitudes, factors such as prior professional experience, high levels of knowledge, and taking courses related to ASD significantly increased professional self-efficacy. Interestingly, first-year students showed higher sensitivity than seniors, possibly reflecting an initial idealistic outlook. In conclusion, while preservice teachers are emotionally prepared and somewhat confident, teacher education programs should emphasize practical experience and evidence-based teaching strategies to bridge the remaining gap between sensitivity and professional self-efficacy in inclusive ASD education.

TI Development of a Risk Warning Indicator System for Depression in
   Children and Adolescents
SO INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF SPECIAL EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE Children; Adolescents; Depression; Risk Warning; Indicator Development
ID SOCIAL SUPPORT; PREVENTION
AB The objective of the study was to create a risk warning indicator system specifically aimed at detecting depression in children and adolescents, facilitating early and precise identification. To establish a preliminary framework for these indicators, the researchers conducted a comprehensive literature review and engaged in expert meetings. The Delphi method was utilized over two rounds of consultations, which helped screen and enhance the proposed indicators. The research team engaged in multiple discussions to refine the outcomes of these consultations, eventually identifying crucial warning indicators. The study evaluated the developed indicators on a cohort of 386 outpatient children and adolescents diagnosed with depression to assess their reliability. Expert response rates in both Delphi rounds were recorded at 100%, with authority coefficients measuring 0.808 and 0.868, respectively. Furthermore, Kendall's coefficient of concordance for the two rounds indicated values of 0.131 and 0.142, both statistically significant (P < 0.001). The finalized risk warning indicator system included five primary indicators and 38 secondary indicators, meeting stringent criteria for effectiveness: a mean importance rating exceeding 3.5, a coefficient of variation below 0.25, and a full-score ratio above 20%. Notably, the content validity index (CVI) for individual items ranged from 0.881 to 1.000, yielding an average CVI of 0.995, while the universal agreement CVI stood at 0.832. The overall reliability of the indicators was substantiated by a KR-20 coefficient of 0.811 and a split-half reliability coefficient of 0.745. In conclusion, the risk warning indicator system developed in this research exhibits robust scientific validity, practicality, and innovative potential, making it a valuable tool for clinical application and broader dissemination in the field of pediatric mental health.

DT Article
DE Youth Civic Engagement; Civil Society; Riverbank Communities;
   Environmental Action; Community Empowerment; Banjarmasin
ID POLITICAL-PARTICIPATION; DIVERSITY; YOUNG
AB Youth civic engagement has increasingly been recognized as a critical driver in strengthening civil society, particularly within marginalized urban communities. In Indonesia, riverbank settlements such as those in Banjarmasin face persistent environmental and social challenges, making them important contexts for examining grassroots civic participation. This study aims to analyze how youth-led civic engagement contributes to the development of civil society in riverbank communities. This research employs a qualitative approach within a constructivist paradigm, utilizing a case study design to explore youth community practices in Banjarmasin. Data were collected through in-depth interviews with youth members aged 18-25 who are actively involved in community initiatives. The data were analyzed using thematic analysis to identify key patterns and meanings related to civic engagement. The findings reveal that youth play a transformative role through (1) environmental civic action, including river clean-up activities and community education; (2) strengthening social cohesion and community empowerment; (3) navigating structural challenges such as limited resources and participation barriers; (4) acting as informal civic educators; and (5) engaging in emerging yet limited institutional collaborations. These activities demonstrate that youth civic engagement operates as both a social and environmental practice that contributes to collective awareness and participatory culture. In conclusion, youth-led initiatives significantly contribute to strengthening civil society in marginalized riverbank areas, although their sustainability depends on stronger institutional support and resource availability. This study highlights the need for policy interventions that recognize and empower youth as key actors in community development. Future research is recommended to adopt comparative and mixed-method approaches to deepen understanding of youth civic engagement across diverse contexts.

TI The Impact of the Student Internship Program on the Skill Development of
   PUP BS Economics Students: A Basis for Curriculum Improvement from the
   Perspective of the Students
SO INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF SPECIAL EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE Internship; Economics Graduates; Skill Development; Curriculum
   Development; Internship Trainers Assessment
AB This study evaluates the impact of internships on skill development and curriculum alignment within the Bachelor of Science in Economics program at the Polytechnic University of the Philippines from the perspective of the student interns. Using a quantitative design, 125 student-interns who completed the Summer 2023-2024 internship course were surveyed with a validated questionnaire covering industry readiness, skills application, course relevance, and perceptions of curriculum improvements. Descriptive statistics revealed that most interns (83.2%) experienced purely onsite placements, received orientation on the organizational mission (96.8%) and structure (95.2%), and achieved clear learning outcomes (88.8%). Supervisory support was universal, with 91.2% reporting regular performance evaluations. Interns rated their industry readiness highly (mean = 4.15/5), especially in ethics, teamwork, and adaptability, while scoring lower in entrepreneurial and leadership competencies. Skill application during internships was also strong (mean = 4.30/5), particularly in professionalism, initiative, and time management, whereas leadership and public speaking were less practiced. Core economics and technical writing courses were considered highly relevant, while general education and advanced mathematics were perceived as moderately or slightly relevant to internship tasks. Independent-samples t-tests indicated no significant differences in readiness based on employer type, commute time, or internship duration, but larger HTEs (>= 200 employees) correlated with greater skill application. Interns supported offering the internship during a single regular semester and increasing the 200-hour requirement. Findings suggest curricular revisions to enhance leadership, entrepreneurship, and communication modules, as well as strengthen partnerships with larger host organizations to optimize student learning outcomes.

TI Impact of Parenting Styles on Parental Mental Health
SO INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF SPECIAL EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE Parenting styles; Parental mental health convergent mixed method design
   parenting styles and dimensions questions; NIMHANS Screening tool for
   psychological problem; emotional regulation
ID STRESS
AB This study utilized a convergent embedded mixed-method design to investigate the relationship between parenting styles and parental mental health among 100 parents (N=100) of children aged six or younger. Using the Parenting Style and Dimensions Questionnaire and NIMHANS Screening Tool for Psychological Problems questionnaire , results revealed a significant positive correlation between authoritative parenting and total distress, and authoritarian parenting and depression. However, parenting styles were poor predictors of mental health outcomes; instead, demographic variables like gender were significant predictors. Significant differences were also noted between mothers and fathers regarding their use of authoritative and authoritarian styles. Qualitative findings from five maternal interviews yielded six themes which emphasised on the distress of the mothers, the reason behind it, its impact on self and others, and the repercussions of the reactions like guilt cycle. , When the quantitative and qualitative findings were integrated, it culminated in an Emotional Regulation Model. This model posits that structural conditions drive emotional dysregulation, which negatively impacts parenting behaviors. This failure to meet parenting ideals triggers a "guilt-repair cycle," ultimately increasing the risk of mental disorders. The study concludes that parental emotional regulation capacity, rather than parenting style alone, is the primary determinant of psychological well-being.

TI Empowering Smart Classroom Efficiency: The Catalytic Role of Academic
   Support in Higher Education
SO INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF SPECIAL EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE Smart Classroom Efficiency; Academic Support; Teacher Factors; Teaching
   Methods; Higher Education
AB While smart classrooms have proliferated in higher education, the mechanisms through which academic support enhances their efficiency remain underexplored. This study investigates the influence of smart classroom (SC), teachers (TE), and teaching methods (TS) on smart classroom efficiency (SCE), and examines the moderating role of academic support (AS) in these relationships. A quantitative survey was conducted with 575 undergraduate students from eight universities in Zhengzhou, China. Data were analyzed using hierarchical regression analysis to test the moderating effects. SC (beta = 0.427, p < 0.001), TE (beta = 0.241, p < 0.001), and TS (beta = 0.151, p = 0.006) significantly influence SCE. Notably, AS significantly moderates all three pathways, with the strongest moderating effect on the TE-SCE relationship (beta = 0.219, p < 0.001). This study advances theoretical understanding of academic support as a catalytic mechanism in technology-enhanced learning environments and provides actionable guidance for designing institutional support systems to maximize smart classroom efficiency.

SO INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF SPECIAL EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE Flipped Classroom; Writing; Meta Analysis
ID HIGHER-EDUCATION
AB In a variety of educational contexts, flipped classrooms have gained popularity as a pedagogical strategy due to the increased interest in active learning strategies. This meta-analysis investigates the effect of flipped classroom model on writing skills. A comprehensive search of academic databases, including Google Scholar, Scopus, and ERIC, was conducted for research published between 2020 and 2023. The analysis focused on studies employing experimental or quasi-experimental designs that met the inclusion criteria for teaching writing through the flipped classroom paradigm. This evidence underscores the potential of flipped instruction to foster improved writing skills among students across diverse educational settings.

   Model for Special Needs Children
SO INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF SPECIAL EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE Adaptive swimming instruction; special needs children; teaching
   framework; teacher development; inclusive education
AB Adaptive swimming instruction for learners with special educational needs requires structured pedagogical guidance that supports teacher competence, decision making, and confidence in real teaching environments. While prior research has demonstrated that the AquaExplorers module improves special education teachers' knowledge and self-confidence in swimming activity management, there remains a need to translate these gains into an operational instructional framework. This study presents the A.S.S.I.S.T. framework, an Adaptive Swimming Support and Instructional Teaching model developed by synthesising empirical findings from two mixed-method and intervention studies on AquaExplorers implementation. The A.S.S.I.S.T. framework extends prior intervention findings by offering a transferable instructional structure that supports inclusive aquatic pedagogy, reduces instructional uncertainty, and strengthens teacher agency. The model has implications for professional development, curriculum design, and adaptive physical education training programmes.

The relationship between resilience and anxiety control shows that resilience functions as a secondary factor while primary mediation remains unfulfilled. findings give crucial information which researchers need to create cognitive-based interventions that will decrease competitive anxiety while improving adaptive functioning.

   Performance
SO INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF SPECIAL EDUCATION

DT Article
DE Assistive Technology; Special Education; Technology Readiness;
   Managerial Capabilities; Sustainability
ID USER ACCEPTANCE; CAPABILITIES; PERSPECTIVE; DISCLOSURE; COUNTRIES; FIRMS
AB This study examines how managerial capabilities influence assistive technology adoption and sustainable performance in special education institutions. Drawing on the Resource-Based View, Stakeholder Theory, and the Technology Acceptance Model, it investigates sustainable education financing, disability-related accounting disclosure, inclusive social marketing orientation, and digital market capability as antecedents of institutional readiness and performance. Data were collected from 312 managerial respondents representing special education institutions in Indonesia and analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling. The results show that sustainable education financing, disability-related accounting disclosure, and inclusive social marketing orientation significantly improve sustainable special education performance, whereas digital market capability has no significant direct effect. However, all four managerial capabilities significantly strengthen assistive technology adoption, which subsequently enhances sustainable performance and mediates the relationship between managerial capabilities and performance. The findings indicate that assistive technology adoption depends not only on resource availability but also on managerial readiness, accountability practices, stakeholder engagement, and digital capacity.

TI Machine Learning Framework for Performance Analysis of Students Using
   Content Recommendation in Education System

DT Article
DE Educational Data Mining; Machine Learning; Student Performance
   Prediction; Content-Based Filtering; Collaborative Filtering; Adaptive
   Learning; LSTM; XGBoost; Personalised Education; Learning Analytics
AB As digital learning environments continue to expand there is a vast amount of information about student interactions-and significant opportunities and challenges for personalised learning. In this paper, a novel framework is presented, called ML-PACS (Machine Learning-based Performance Analysis and Content Suggestion), which comprises an ensemble learning, deep learning and a hybrid collaborative-content-based filtering to simultaneously predict student academic performance and suggest content for students in a context-aware way. The framework receives data streams which are heterogeneous like previous academic records, Logs from Learning Management System (LMS), Quiz and Assignment scores, Learning style indicators, Peer interaction metric. The stacked ensemble of three classifiers: XGBoost, Random Forest and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks obtained an accuracy of 92.8%, an F1 score of 91.2%, a precision of 91.6%, and a recall of 90.9% with 2400 learners across six semesters. The best Hit Rate@10 (83.9%) and NDCG@10 (0.567) among all the baseline methods are achieved by the recommendation module with a performance-aware hybrid filter with the prediction of the performance tier as a contextual signal. The results of the longitudinal evaluation reveal that there is a different average score for the experimental and control groups for the three academic years evaluated, showing an improvement of 80.1% in the experimental group and 62.0% in the control group. The suggested model provides specific recommendations to the teachers who have automated alert systems and visual dashboards, for early pedagogical interventions. Results reveal that, when predictive analytics is used alongside adaptive content recommendation, students' outcomes measurably improve in the long run.

TI Management Strategy of Inclusive Education in Indonesian Junior High
   Schools: Voices from Teachers and School Leaders
SO INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF SPECIAL EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE Inclusive education; junior high school; management strategy;
   qualitative study
AB Inclusive education in Indonesia faces complex challenges that require a strategic approach and a thorough understanding. Although many studies have addressed aspects such as teacher attitudes and the role of parents, research that discusses on an inclusive education strategy management remains limited. Using Wheelen et al., (2021)'s framework, this study investigates the teachers and school leaders' perceptions of the inclusive education management strategy in two junior high schools in Bandarlampung, Indonesia. The data for this descriptive qualitative research were obtained through in-depth interviews. The results show five main strategies: 1) environmental scanning, internal and external environmental analysis through a SWOT analysis; 2) formulation of strategies that include vision, mission, and short-medium-long term planning; 3) implementation of strategies through inclusion policies, teacher training, socialization, budget allocation, and motivation for inclusion students; and 4) strategy evaluation through data measurement and analysis, and 5) modification as the feedback to ensure that the implemented strategy remains relevant and effective. These findings suggest that schools develop a comprehensive inclusion management strategy that involves all stakeholders. Teachers are expected to play an active role in creating a collaborative learning environment and supporting the success of inclusive education in a sustainable manner.

TI AI-Driven Dynamic Reorder Point Prediction for Inventory Management in
   Supply Chains: A Machine Learning Approach
SO INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF SPECIAL EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE Dynamic Reorder Point; Inventory Management; Machine Learning; Supply
   Chain Analytics; Demand Forecasting; Stockout Reduction; Safety Stock;
   Retail Transactions
AB Keeping the right amount of stock in a modern supply chain is a tricky balancing act. It comes down to making sure products are there when people want them without spending a fortune on warehouse space, all while demand shifts and changes in ways that are hard to pin down. Most places still use old-school reorder point methods. These work fine enough, but they usually bank on everything staying the same, which just isn't how retail works anymore. This research looks into how AI might handle those shifting numbers better by creating dynamic reorder points based on actual retail transaction data. It involved building a specific pipeline to turn messy sales records into clear demand patterns for individual items, then testing out various machine learning models to see if they could actually predict what happens next. Those predictions were then plugged into a system designed to adjust reorder levels on the fly and tested in a simulated environment. The numbers show that machine learning does a much better job of guessing demand than the basic statistical shortcuts people used to rely on. When these models were used to set reorder points, the system got much better at preventing empty shelves and keeping customers happy. But there is a catch. Better service usually meant holding onto more stock, which points to a clear tension between being reliable and being cheap. Looking closer at the data, it became obvious that how long it takes for a shipment to arrive really changes how well these policies work. Plus, even the smartest models struggled when demand went totally off the rails or when weird, one-off transactions popped up. In the end, it seems that using Machine Learning to move reorder points around can actually help a business run better, provided the system is set up thoughtfully. This work offers a clear, repeatable way to link demand guesses with inventory simulations, giving a solid starting point for anyone trying to build better decision tools for supply chains. It also serves as a reminder that a more accurate forecast only matters if it actually leads to a smarter decision on the warehouse floor.

TI Usability, Pedagogical Effectiveness, and Student Experience in a
   VR-Based Motor Skills Program for Special Educational Needs: Findings
   from an Erasmus+ Project
SO INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF SPECIAL EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE virtual reality; motor skills; special educational needs (SEN);
   inclusive education; pedagogical effectiveness
ID VIRTUAL-REALITY; FINE; CHILDREN
AB Motor skills are essential for children's educational development, facilitating literacy, executive functioning, attention, and social integration. For children with special educational needs (SEN), motor difficulties frequently co-occur with other neurodevelopmental challenges, exacerbating barriers to inclusive learning environments. In response to these challenges, this study assessed a virtual reality (VR) motor skills training program developed by the Erasmus+ project and implemented across Turkiye, Greece, Spain, and Poland. A quantitative, cross-sectional survey design was employed using data from educators and students involved in the project's training and implementation phases. Three instruments were used to collect data: a workshop evaluation scale completed by educators following professional development training, a teacher evaluation form administered after program implementation, and a student feedback form completed by SEN students. The findings indicate that educators generally perceived the training process and VR-based intervention positively, particularly regarding pedagogical value, student engagement, and support for motor development. However, concerns were raised about the relevance of certain training components and the technology's usability, especially its ease of use in classroom settings. Students reported high levels of enjoyment and engagement with the VR activities, suggesting strong acceptance of the intervention, although variations in selfconfidence were noted. The results suggest that VR-based motor skills training holds significant promise as an engaging and pedagogically valuable tool for SEN education. Nevertheless, its effectiveness appears to depend on usability, contextual adaptation, and the quality of implementation. Future research should incorporate objective motor performance measures and longitudinal designs to understand better the sustained impact of VR-based interventions in inclusive educational contexts.

TI From Isolation to Influence: Examining the Impact of a Statewide Virtual
   Professional Learning Community on Special Education Professionals

AB The MITTIN Project is a virtual learning library designed to strengthen independent living skills for students with moderate-to-severe disabilities. Virtual PLCs were launched to support the implementation of the interactive mixed-reality instructional modules. While prior research has demonstrated the impact of PLCs on instructional practice, less is known about their influence on educators' professional growth, leadership development, and career trajectories, particularly in special education contexts. TI A Proposed Structural Model for the Relationship between Research
   Anxiety and Academic Perfectionism among University Students
SO INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF SPECIAL EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE Research anxiety; academic perfectionism; university students;
   regression analysis; psychological factors
ID COGNITIVE PERFORMANCE; STRESS; SELF
AB University students experience research anxiety as a significant academic challenge that can negatively affect engagement and performance. Academic perfectionism has been identified as a central cognitive factor influencing students' emotional experiences in academic contexts. This study investigated the relationship between academic perfectionism and research anxiety and examined dimension-specific predictive effects among university students. A quantitative cross-sectional design was employed with a sample of 380 psychology students, and data were collected using standardized self-report instruments. Statistical analysis included descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, and multiple regression, with path coefficients estimated using AMOS software; however, no latent-variable path analysis with fit indices was conducted. The results indicated that participants reported moderate levels of research anxiety (M = 2.51) and high levels of academic perfectionism (M = 3.97). As hypothesized, the global correlation between the two constructs was weak and non-significant (r = .074, p = .149). Multiple regression analysis explained 14.4% of the variance in research anxiety (R-2 = .144). Doubts about actions significantly predicted higher research anxiety (beta = .270, p < .001), whereas self-oriented perfectionism significantly predicted lower research anxiety (beta = -.252, p < .001). Other dimensions (self-criticism, socially prescribed perfectionism, self-worth contingency) were not statistically significant predictors. These findings indicate that academic perfectionism does not demonstrate a meaningful global relationship with research anxiety, but its dimensions exhibit opposing effects. Total perfectionism scores should not be used to predict research anxiety.

LA English
DT Article

AB Under the background of cross-cultural education and global mobility, the unique geographical environment and cultural characteristics of Heilongjiang Province pose complex challenges to the academic adaptation of international students. This study aims to explore the influence path of social support on the academic performance of international students and focuses on examining the mediating role of academic self-efficacy in this process. Through conducting a questionnaire survey among 509 international students in colleges and universities in Heilongjiang Province, and using Amos 26.0 to construct a structural equation model (SEM) for empirical analysis. This research theoretically deepens the application logic of social cognitive theory in extremely objective environments. TI Early Childhood Education Practices for Learners with Down Syndrome
SO INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF SPECIAL EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE Down Syndrome; Early Childhood Education; Home preparation; Transition
   support; Inclusive Education
ID CHILDREN; HOME
AB The transition from home to school is crucial for learners with Down Syndrome, involving navigating routine and expectation changes, often worsened by cognitive and adaptive challenges. Given limited resources in South African schools, early home routines and rules are crucial to support learners and ease their transition to school. To investigate how home-based prep, routines, rules, and demonstrations impact learners with Down Syndrome transitioning to early childhood education. A qualitative study consisting of N = 3 participants was conducted at a special needs school in Gauteng. A qualitative case study within an interpretivist paradigm was employed. Data were gathered through semi-structured and narrative interviews with parents, teachers and school management, alongside document analysis of inclusive education policies. Thematic analysis methods to identify key patterns. Four core themes emerged: (1) Establishing predictable home routines to support school readiness, (2) Use of clear and consistent rules to promote behavioural adjustment, (3) Hands-on demonstration as a primary learning strategy at home, and (4) Family support as a foundation for resilience during transition. This study affirms that home-based preparation, through routines, clear rules, and demonstrations, is crucial for a successful transition to early childhood education for learners with Down Syndrome. Supporting families as primary agents of early transition is crucial for learners with Down Syndrome, emphasising the importance of early engagement and home preparation in school readiness. This study emphasises the importance of home-based prep and family support in helping children with Down syndrome make successful transitions.

ID PEDAGOGICAL CONTENT KNOWLEDGE
AB The increasing integration of digital technologies in higher education has raised expectations for language teachers to develop strong digital competence to support technology-enhanced learning environments. However, empirical evidence regarding whether teachers' digital competence contributes to teaching effectiveness remains limited. This study therefore examined the relationship between EFL teachers' digital competence and their teaching effectiveness. A quantitative correlational research design was employed. Data were collected from 879 EFL lecturers working in Vietnam. Pearson product-moment correlation analysis was conducted to examine the relationship between the two constructs. The findings indicated that lecturers reported relatively high levels of both digital competence and teaching effectiveness across most dimensions. However, the correlation analysis revealed that digital competence did not have a significant relationship with teaching effectiveness. These findings suggest that digital competence alone may not necessarily lead to improved teaching performance. To explain this result, the study proposes an interpretive perspective in which the influence of digital competence operates indirectly through the pedagogical integration of digital technologies, while institutional factors such as technological infrastructure, professional development opportunities, and technical support also shape instructional effectiveness. The study highlights the complex and context-dependent nature of technology integration in EFL higher education.

   English to Hindi Machine Translation Perspective

LA English
DT Article

   Metrices; Machine; Translation; Precision and Recall; Natural Language
   Processing
AB Background: Recognizing the incompatibility of traditional or generalpurpose automatic evaluation metrices in measuring the pronoun translation quality of a machine translation output (MTO), researchers evolved some pronoun specific metrices to measure the pronoun translation quality. From this point of view, this research paper is aimed: (i) to have a systematic study about such pronoun specific evaluation metrices, (ii) to check their suitability for an English to Hindi machine translation (EHMT) system and (iii) to perform an empirical analysis of these metrices with respect to an EHMT system. Method: Accounting to three major selection criteria viz. ease of implementation, language independent methodology and scope of performance enhancement, related literature was explored and surveyed. Conclusion: Study and analysis revealed that PRF and APT both metrices are enough suitable for an EHMT system and can be adapted with certain language specific modifications. Experiment results are quite encouraging and show that with accurate word alignment, appropriate configuration setting and case wise weight assignment, APT metric outperform over PRF.

LA English
DT Article
DE Teacher Professionalism; School Resources; Self Efficacy; Students Vocal
   Performance Ability; Music College Students
ID THEATER
AB This study focuses on the broader context of Chengdu's development as an international music capital and aims to analyze the underlying mechanisms driving the improvement of performance skills among college students majoring in vocal music. By constructing a path model linking environmental factors to individual psychological variables, the study conducted a questionnaire survey of vocal music students at multiple universities in Chengdu and performed rigorous statistical analyses using structural equation modeling (SEM).The findings reveal that both teachers' professional competence and institutional resources exert significant positive predictive effects on vocal performance ability, with the direct influence of institutional resources being particularly pronounced. TI Evolution of Research on Socio-Emotional Learning and Career Readiness
   among Autistic Adolescents: A Bibliometric Analysis from 2000 to 2025
SO INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF SPECIAL EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE Bibliometric analysis; Autistic adolescents; Socio-emotional
   development; Career Readiness; Trends
ID SPECTRUM DISORDERS; EMPLOYMENT; TRANSITION; EDUCATION; YOUTH
AB Socio-emotional learning and career readiness are increasingly recognised as critical components in supporting autistic adolescents during the transition to adulthood. This bibliometric study examined the evolution of research in this field between 2000 and 2025 using data retrieved from the Scopus database and analysed through VOSviewer 1.6.20. A total of 222 records were initially identified, of which 71 relevant articles were retained following the screening and eligibility assessment process based on predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria. The findings indicate a substantial increase in publication output after 2015, reflecting growing scholarly attention toward mental health, emotional regulation, transition-to-work pathways, and psychosocial support for autistic youth. The United States and the United Kingdom emerged as the most influential contributors, demonstrating strong international collaboration networks with researchers across Europe, Australia and selected Asian countries. Source analysis identified leading journals such as the Journal of Autism and Developmental Disorders, Autism and Research in Developmental Disabilities as dominant publication outlets shaping the intellectual structure of the field. Keyword co-occurrence analysis revealed major thematic clusters related to mental health, social participation, transition planning, employment readiness, family support and intervention-based practices. The findings further suggest that the field has evolved from deficit-oriented perspectives toward more ecological and participation-focused approaches to autism transition research. Nevertheless, the literature remains geographically imbalanced, with limited representation from Asian and Global South contexts. Overall, this study provides a comprehensive overview of publication trends, collaborative structures and emerging research themes while highlighting the need for culturally responsive and contextually grounded research to support equitable transition outcomes for autistic adolescents.

TI Hybrid Edge-Cloud Intelligent Assistive Framework for Inclusive
   Industrial Training and Adaptive Quality Monitoring
SO INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF SPECIAL EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE Assistive Intelligent Systems; Inclusive Industrial Training; Adaptive
   Learning; Deep Reinforcement Learning; Disability-Support Automation;
   AI-Enabled Monitoring
AB Accessible vocational training for individuals with disabilities demands intelligent, real-time systems capable of adaptive, personalised support within complex industrial environments. The Hybrid Edge-Cloud Intelligent Assistive Framework (ECIAF) in this work is a specific purposebuilt design that combines low-latency edge-based visual monitoring with cloud-hosted deep reinforcement learning for scalable, responsive assistive support for technically disadvantaged learners and workers. The edge tier implemented using a lightweight ResNet-18 convolutional model achieves an average inference latency of 11.90 ms and defect detection accuracy of 97.20% on the MVTec AD benchmark, significantly exceeding real-time responsiveness requirements for assistive purposes. The cloud tier uses a Deep Q-Network (DQN) agent that is trained using a logistic regression environment model adapted from the SECOM semiconductor manufacturing dataset to dynamically calibrate ten process-support parameters representative of scaffolding level, task complexity, and feedback intensity in inclusive education. The adaptive support mechanism in more than 500 training episodes achieved a near-zero error rate, achieving a 99.96% reduction in monitored task errors, surpassing all defined inclusive training objectives. The tri-tiered architecture of the framework-perception, adaptive intelligence and an accessible multimodal interface-is tightly integrated with Universal Design for Learning principles and assistive technology design standards, enabling support for a wide range of cognitive, sensory and physical disabilities. The study highlights the ECIAF as a technologically sound and pedagogically grounded basis for future inclusive industrial education systems.

TI Prevalence of Musculoskeletal Pain and Associated Factors among
   Undergraduate Medical Students of Merit University, Sohag, Egypt
SO INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF SPECIAL EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE Musculoskeletal pain; Undergraduate; Physical therapy student; Other
   medical students; Neck pain
ID LOW-BACK-PAIN; SHOULDER SYMPTOMS; RISK-FACTORS; NECK; EPIDEMIOLOGY;
   DISORDERS; CHILDREN
AB Aim: This study aimed to explore the prevalence and determinants of musculoskeletal pain (MSP) among undergraduate medical students and compare the findings across physiotherapy, medicine, and pharmacy faculties. Subject and Methods: A cross-sectional study was conducted from August 2023 to February 2024 among 252 female students at Merit University. A structured questionnaire was used, incorporating the Nordic Musculoskeletal Questionnaire (NMQ) and the Global Physical Activity Questionnaire (GPAQ), to evaluate the presence, location, and severity of MSP. Demographic data, body mass index (BMI), and study habits were also collected. Results: The prevalence of MSP was notably high, particularly in the neck and lower back regions. Female students and physiotherapy students in years beyond the first year reported significantly higher rates of pain. A positive correlation was observed between higher BMI, prolonged poor postures during lectures and study sessions, and increased MSP. However, there was no statistically significant difference in MSP prevalence between physiotherapy and other medical students overall. Conclusion: The high prevalence of musculoskeletal pain among female medical students calls for further ergonomic research and clinical evaluation. Medical schools should address MSP by improving seating arrangements and educating students on lifestyle modifications for MSP prevention.

TI Mechanism-Based Model of Teacher Competence: Explaining How
   Instructional Practices and Contextual Support Shape the Socio-Emotional
   Development of Students with Dyslexia
SO INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF SPECIAL EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE Dyslexia; Teacher competence; Socio-emotional development; Instructional
   practices; Teacher self-efficacy
ID ADOLESCENTS
AB Dyslexia is increasingly recognised as a learning difficulty that also carries important socio-emotional implications. However, research on teacher competence remains fragmented and mainly descriptive, with limited explanation of how teacher competence shapes students' socioemotional development. To address this gap, this study conducted a systematic literature review of empirical studies published between 2022 and 2025 on teacher competence in supporting the socioemotional development of students with dyslexia. Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, 21 studies were systematically identified and synthesised using a thematic approach. The findings conceptualise teacher competence as a dynamic and multidimensional construct comprising knowledge, instructional practices, socio-emotional responsiveness, and professional self-efficacy. The analysis further identifies instructional practices as the primary mechanism through which professional competence influences socio-emotional outcomes, while contextual factors, including intervention programmes and school-level support, shape the strength of this relationship. Based on this synthesis, the study proposes a mechanism-based explanatory model that advances existing literature by shifting the focus from domain-based descriptions to a process-oriented understanding of teacher competence. The findings contribute to theory by offering a dynamic and context-sensitive framework, while also providing practical implications for teacher education, classroom practice, and policy development in special education.

TI Social Media Dependency and English-Speaking Performance in Mock Job
   Interviews among Filipino Pre-Service Teachers in an Inclusive
   University Context
SO INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF SPECIAL EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE social media dependency; communicative competence; pre-service teachers;
   mock job interview; English speaking performance
AB The increasing integration of digital technology into students' daily lives has raised concerns about its potential impact on academic and communicative performance. In particular, social media dependency among pre-service teachers may influence their ability to perform effectively in formal speaking tasks such as job interviews. This study examined the relationship between social media dependency and English-speaking performance in mock job interviews among Filipino freshman pre-service teachers in an inclusive university context. The study employed a mixed-methods design, specifically an explanatory sequential approach. A total of 43 valid respondents were included in the final analysis. Data were gathered using a researcher-adapted Social Media Dependency Questionnaire, a structured mock job interview, and a speaking performance rubric assessing fluency, grammatical accuracy, coherence, and pragmatic competence. Quantitative data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and Pearson correlation, while qualitative data from interview transcripts were examined through discourse analysis. Results revealed that participants exhibited a high level of social media dependency and a moderate level of speaking performance in mock job interviews. Furthermore, findings showed a significant moderate negative relationship between social media dependency and speaking performance, indicating that higher dependency is associated with lower oral communication competence. Additionally, students who performed better in qualifying examinations showed slightly higher speaking scores; however, overall communicative competence remained moderate across groups. The study concludes that while pre-service teachers meet academic qualification standards, their communicative competence in English-speaking tasks remains insufficient for professional demands. It recommends the integration of structured oral communication training and responsible digital literacy programs within teacher education curricula to enhance students' readiness for professional communication.

TI A Watermarking-Assisted Framework for Secure Sharing of QR-Linked
   Digital Learning Resources in Inclusive Education
SO INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF SPECIAL EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE inclusive education; digital learning resources; QR code; invisible
   watermarking; image authentication; secure sharing; content integrity
AB Digital learning resources such as worksheets, visual aids, annotated diagrams, and QR-linked instructional materials are increasingly shared through mobile platforms and messaging applications in inclusive education contexts. During repeated sharing, these resources may undergo compression, resizing, or format conversion, which can make their origin difficult to verify and may allow unauthorized modification or redistribution to go unnoticed. This paper proposes an invisible QR watermarking-assisted framework for authentication and secure sharing of digital learning resources. Instead of encoding the complete document into a QR code, the proposed framework encodes compact authentication metadata, such as document identifier, institution ID, timestamp, verification URL, and resource hash, into a full-color QR payload. The QR payload is then invisibly embedded into the educational image or document-page image using a deep learning-based watermarking encoder. After transmission through compression-prone platforms, including WhatsApp image-mode sharing, a restoration module is applied before QR payload recovery. Experimental evaluation on a held-out validation set of 500 images shows that the watermarked images maintain acceptable visual quality, with PSNR of 31.02 +/- 0.97 dB and SSIM of 0.9169 +/- 0.0224. Real WhatsApp image-mode validation on the same 500 transmitted images achieved an Enhanced Scan Success Rate of 82.8% and a Direct Scan Success Rate of 57.8% when the restoration module was active. Without the restoration module, both scan success rates were 0%. These results indicate the technical feasibility of the proposed framework for source verification and traceability of shared digital learning resources. The study does not evaluate classroom learning outcomes or learner-level educational impact; its contribution is limited to secure sharing, content integrity, and source authentication of QR-linked digital learning resources.

TI The Influence of Educational Content on Social Media on Junior High
   School Student Understanding and Behavior Regarding Birth Rate Control
SO INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF SPECIAL EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE educational content; social media; students' understanding; behavior;
   birth rate control
AB This study aims to examine the influence of educational content on social media on the understanding and behavior of junior high school (Sekolah Menengah Pertama/SMP) students regarding birth rate control. The study employed a quantitative approach using a survey method, in which questionnaires were distributed to 70 students from grades VII, VIII, and IX. The collected data were analyzed using several statistical tests, including validity and reliability tests, Pearson correlation, simple linear regression, ANOVA, and t-tests. The results indicate that educational content on social media has a significant influence on students' understanding and behavior, with a correlation coefficient of 0.516 and a significance level of 0.000. Linear regression analysis shows that approximately 26.6% of the variation in students' behavior can be explained by their level of understanding of information obtained through social media. The results of the ANOVA and t-tests reveal no significant differences based on grade level or gender. These findings suggest that social media serves as an effective and equitable educational tool in shaping students' awareness and positive behavior regarding the importance of birth rate control.

   for Students with Autism in Inclusive Secondary Education: Experts' and
   Teachers' Perspectives

LA English
DT Article
DE Social Interaction Skills; Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD); Inclusive
   Secondary Education; Needs Analysis; Module Development; Design and
   Development Research (DDR)
AB This study was conducted to analyze the needs for the design and development of a teaching module on social interaction skills for students with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) in inclusive secondary education. Although inclusive education has been increasingly implemented, there remains a lack of systematic, structured, and contextualised modules. This study employed the Design and Development Research (DDR) approach, guided by the ADDIE model with a focus on the needs analysis phase. Data were collected through questionnaires involving three experts and semi-structured interviews with five teachers, and were analysed using descriptive and thematic analysis. The findings show that experts demonstrated a high level of agreement, with percentages ranging from 67% to 100% regarding the need for the module. Thematic analysis identified four main themes: teachers' professional needs, module requirements, instructional strategies, and implementation constraints. Teachers also reported a lack of specialised training and the absence of structured guidelines. The proposed module should emphasise social awareness, emotional regulation, communication, and social interaction through strategies such as role-playing, peer-mediated approaches, scaffolding, and visual supports. This study highlights the need for a contextualised and theory-based module to enhance social skills and self-confidence among students with ASD.

TI Predicting Student Outcomes in Special Education: The Role of Teacher
   Well-Being Dimensions through Multiple Regression Analysis
SO INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF SPECIAL EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE Special education teacher well-being; students with special educational
   needs (SEN); student outcomes; multiple regression analysis; school
   environment
AB Teacher well-being has been identified as a critical yet empirically underexamined determinant of instructional quality in special education, particularly within Asian contexts. Grounded in Allardt's Sociological Welfare Theory (1989) and Bloom's Taxonomy (Bloom et al., 1956), this quantitative survey study examined the level of teacher well-being, its relationship with, and predictive influence on the outcomes of students with special educational needs (SEN) among 437 primary school special education teachers in Peninsular Malaysia, selected through multistage sampling. Descriptive findings indicated that overall teacher well-being was at a very high level (M = 4.23, SD = 0.44), with self-achievement (M = 4.27) and health (M = 4.25) rated very high, while school environmental conditions were rated high (M = 4.18). Pearson correlation analysis revealed a strong, positive, and statistically significant relationship between teacher well-being and SEN student outcomes (r = .692, p < .01), reflecting a large effect size. Multiple regression analysis further demonstrated that all three dimensions of teacher well-being significantly predicted SEN student outcomes, with school environmental conditions emerging as the strongest predictor (beta = .341, p < .001), followed by self-achievement (beta = .257, p < .001) and health (beta = .196, p < .001). The model collectively accounted for 48.1% of the variance in SEN student outcomes (R-2 = .481, adjusted R-2 = .477), indicating substantial predictive power. These findings suggest that structural and environmental factors exert greater influence on SEN student outcomes than individual-level well-being attributes, underscoring the need for targeted investment in school infrastructure, teacher professional development, and institutional well-being support mechanisms within Malaysian special education settings.

TI A CNN-Based Hybrid Approach for Semantic Textual Similarity in
   Kannada-English Language Pair
SO INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF SPECIAL EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE Natural Language Processing (NLP); Semantic Textual Similarity (STS);
   Word Embeddings; Stop-word removal; Part-of-Speech Tagging; Word Sense
   Disambiguation (WSD)
ID WORD; FRAMEWORK
AB Semantic similarity estimation across a pair sentence is one among the major concerns for NLP, and Information retrieval, machine translation, text summarization, and automatic evaluation are just a few of its many uses. While much work has been done in monolingual settings, (STS) cross-lingual semantic textual similarity remains an open issue, particularly when considering low-resource language pairs such as Kannada-English. This research proposes a semantic textual similarity assessment method using a hybrid technique of a brief English and Kannada text sentence pairs by considering lexical, syntactic, and semantic aspects. The approach incorporates word-based similarity measures along with lexical resources and vector-based similarity measures along with word embeddings. Cross-lingual word embedding alignment is done by utilizing VecMap and MUSE. A lexical decomposition approach is used to decompose similar and dissimilar semantic components. Similarity in word order is incorporated to record syntactic structure. Finally, a scoring-level fusion method is employed to generate similarity score. Moreover, CNN model is also applied for better classification results. Efficiency of the model is evaluated based on Samanantar Parallel Corpus, which contains sentence pairs in different languages generated through AI4Bharat.The hybrid method outperforms the standard word-level and embedding-level techniques, as shown in the experimental results. Furthermore, It has been noted that the embedding alignment approach performs better as the size of the bilingual dictionaries, and MUSE outperforms other techniques for large dictionaries. The proposed framework is effective for cross-lingual semantic similarity measurement in low-resource scenarios and can be extended to other multilingual tasks pertaining to NLP such as automatic grading, translation systems in machines, and cross-language IR systems.

TI Prevalence & Determinants of Low Testosterone Levels in Men with Type 2
   Diabetes Mellitus Presenting to a Tertiary Care Hospital
SO INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF SPECIAL EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE Hypogonadism; Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus; Testosterone; Erectile
   Dysfunction; SHIM Scale; Prevalence
ID LUTEINIZING-HORMONE; SEXUAL FUNCTION; RISK-FACTORS; THERAPY; DEFICIENCY;
   METAANALYSIS; DYSFUNCTION; ORIGINS; OBESITY; INDEX
AB Introduction: The association between Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (T2DM) and male hypogonadism is increasingly recognized. However, data regarding its prevalence and determinants remain limited in certain populations. Understanding this relationship is essential for improving comprehensive diabetic care and addressing associated complications such as erectile dysfunction and reduced quality of life. Aim & Objective: The study aimed to assess the prevalence and determinants of low testosterone (LowT) in men with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (T2DM). It included evaluation of erectile dysfunction (ED) using the SHIM scale, identification of potential predictors such as body mass index (BMI) and lifestyle factors, and determination of the association between diabetic status and testosterone levels. Materials & Methods: A cross-sectional study was conducted over 18 months at a tertiary care hospital in Chennai. A total of 329 patients with T2DM were recruited using purposive sampling. Data collection included demographic details, clinical history, and assessment of erectile dysfunction using the SHIM questionnaire. Laboratory investigations measured serum total, free, and bioavailable testosterone levels. Statistical analysis was performed using SPSS version 21. Results: The prevalence of LowT was 74.8%. Erectile dysfunction was observed in 94.2% of participants, with severity significantly associated with LowT (p < 0.001). No significant associations were found between LowT and age, occupation, smoking, alcohol consumption, physical activity, BMI, or glycemic parameters (fasting plasma glucose and HbA1c). However, strong associations were noted between LowT and psychological, somatic, and sexual symptom severity (p < 0.001). Waist circumference showed a trend toward association (p = 0.068). Conclusion: There is a high prevalence of hypogonadism and erectile dysfunction among men with T2DM. Testosterone deficiency is strongly associated with symptom severity but not with conventional metabolic or lifestyle factors alone. Routine screening for hypogonadism should be incorporated into the management of diabetic men to improve overall quality of life.

TI Contemporary Vocal and Choral Performance: Trends and Insights
SO INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF SPECIAL EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE vocal and choral performance; sacred music; liturgical singing;
   conducting competitions; performing interpretation; choir in the
   theater; national identity; genre synthesis; actor's singing;
   universalization of the actor
AB The presented research examines the dynamic landscape of Ukrainian vocal and choral performance through the prism of artistic challenges and transformations of the 21st century. The authors focus on the multifaceted nature of the genre, where the regeneration of archaic layers of Orthodox spiritual singing organically intertwines with practices of historically informed performance and bold experiments based on modern dramatic theater. Special emphasis is placed on the conceptual change in the functions of the choir in the theatrical space: today it is not just a static background, but a full-fledged acting subject that operates with a synthesis of academic vocals, historically informed performance, folklore authenticity, and pop manners. The article proves that the modern stage dictates a request for the universalization of the performer and active diffusion with digital technologies. At the same time, analyzing the experience of the 2024 conductor competitions, the researchers substantiate the phenomenon of choral consolidation as a strategic response of the artistic community to the challenges of war. As a result, vocal and choral art appears as a flexible system that preserves the national code, adapting to the demands of the time.

TI Digital Transformation of Education: Discourse on the Digital
   Technologies Effectiveness in Distance Learning
SO INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF SPECIAL EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE digital maturity; hybrid learning; educational modeling; digital
   pedagogy; learning management systems
AB The rapid digital transformation of education significantly reshaped pedagogical practices and institutional strategies, particularly within the context of distance learning. While digital technologies are widely recognized as key drivers of educational innovation, their effectiveness remains dependent on the alignment between technological infrastructure, pedagogical design, and institutional readiness. This study aims to analyze the effectiveness of digital technologies in distance learning and to develop a conceptual model for evaluating their impact within digitally transforming educational environments. The research employs an integrative review methodology to synthesize contemporary theoretical and empirical studies on digital transformation in education. The review identifies major thematic directions in recent scholarly discourse, including the transition from digitization to digital transformation, the increasing role of hybrid learning models, and the growing importance of personalized learning environments. Based on the synthesized findings, a conceptual evaluation model was developed by integrating the logic of digital maturity progression with a strategic matrix-based analytical approach. The proposed model distinguishes between digitization, digitalization, and digital transformation as sequential stages of institutional development and maps these stages against indicators of pedagogical effectiveness. This framework enables the identification of developmental trajectories and supports systematic assessment of digital learning environments. The study contributes to the theoretical understanding of digital transformation in education and provides practical guidance for institutions seeking to enhance the effectiveness of digital technologies in distance learning. Future research directions include empirical validation of the model across diverse educational contexts.

TI Writing for Research Publications in Digitally Enhanced Learning
   Environments
SO INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF SPECIAL EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE Digital scholarship; Artificial intelligence literacy; Academic
   productivity; Research workflows; Knowledge synthesis tools; Learning
   analytics; Scholarly communication; Human-AI collaboration
ID JOURNALS
AB The rapid development of digitally enhanced learning environments has significantly transformed academic writing practices and scholarly communication processes. This study investigates the evolving nature of writing for research publications in digitally mediated settings, with particular attention to the role of artificial intelligence tools and digital competence development. A bibliometric and conceptual analysis approach was employed to identify dominant thematic clusters and structural relationships within contemporary research literature. The findings reveal four key domains shaping modern academic writing: digitally enhanced learning environments, AI-supported writing technologies, digital competence and AI literacy, and scholarly communication productivity. The study proposes an integrative conceptual framework that conceptualizes research writing as a multi-layered socio-technical system involving digital infrastructure, AI-mediated processes, cognitive competencies, and scholarly outputs. Case-based insights derived from emerging research-support tools such as Consensus and SciSpace illustrate practical transformations in literature discovery, content synthesis, and manuscript preparation. The results highlight both the opportunities and risks associated with AI integration, emphasizing the importance of critical evaluation skills and ethical awareness. The study contributes to theoretical and practical understanding of digital scholarly communication and provides recommendations for enhancing research productivity in technologically advanced learning environments.

TI Enhancing Intercultural Communication Competence through Situated
   Learning: A Mixed-Methods Study of International Students in Taiwan
SO JOURNAL OF INTERNATIONAL STUDENTS
LA English
DT Article
DE Cognitive Disequilibrium; Intercultural Adjustment; Intercultural
   Communication Competence; International Students; Mixed Methods;
   Situated Learning; Transformative Learning
ID ADAPTATION
AB This study investigated the development of intercultural communication competence (ICC) among international students in Taiwan, examining the role of situated learning in fostering adaptation within authentic, nonclassroom contexts. A convergent parallel mixed-methods design was employed across two student cohorts. Quantitative data were collected through pre-and post-surveys using the IntegratedModel ofIntercultural Communication Competence (IMICC) and the Intercultural Adjustment Potential Scale (ICAPS). Qualitative data were gathered from students' reflective journals, posters, and semistructured interviews. In a two-phase study structure, the first phase implemented a sequential situated learning experience, while the second phase compared the effects of direct (market visits) and indirect (documentary viewing) situated learning approaches. Quantitative findings revealed a modest overall increase in students' self-assessed ICCs but a notable decrease in the cognitive competence subscale. Thematic analysis of the qualitative data explained this paradox, identifying cognitive disequilibrium as the central mechanism of development. Students' prior assumptions were destabilized, leading to a critical shift from unconscious to conscious incompetence. The study concludes that ICC development is a nonlinear process catalyzed by the productive struggle of cognitive disequilibrium. Situated learning effectively facilitates this by immersing students in authentic challenges that dismantle oversimplified cultural assumptions. Pedagogical implications for designing intercultural curricula that embrace productive disequilibrium are discussed.

TI Navigating Cultural Transition: Experiences of International Students at
   a Midwestern University
SO JOURNAL OF INTERNATIONAL STUDENTS
LA English
DT Article
DE Acculturation; Cultural transition; Institutional support; International
   students; Qualitative research
ID ACCULTURATION; SENSE
AB International students make a remarkable contribution to U.S. higher education, but face considerable obstacles during cultural transition. This qualitative study investigated the cultural adaptation experiences of 15 international students at a midwestern university, led by Berry's acculturation theory. Data from semistructured interviews were analyzed using thematic analysis. The findings revealed that students navigated significant academic and linguistic challenges and adapted a twofold social network, primarily relying on conational peers before seeking cross-cultural connections. While centralized services were valuable, personalized faculty mentorship and peer relationships were the most effective supports, facilitating a shift toward a bicultural identity. The study concludes that successful integration requires a "whole-of-university" approach, implying a need for enhanced peer mentoring and faculty development to foster more inclusive and supportive campus environments.

TI Impact of attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) on academic

   comparative cross-sectional study
SO REVISTA ELECTRONICA CALIDAD EN LA EDUCACION SUPERIOR
LA Spanish
DT Article
DE Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder; academic performance;
   university students; Physical Therapy
AB Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD), although commonly linked to childhood, persistsintoadulthood and affects university academic performance. This cross-sectional comparative study analyzed the relationship between ADHD and academic achievement among Physical Therapy students in Ecuador, a degree with high cognitive, practical, and communicative demands. A total of 324 students fromsecond to ninth levels, all over 18 years old, were randomly selected. Findings revealed that 11.1% (n=36) hada confirmed diagnosis, and 83.3% of them were not receiving treatment. Students with ADHD presented lower grade point averages (p=0.004), higherrates of semester repetition (p=0.018), and difficulties in concentration and organization. It was concluded that ADHD is a risk factor that requirestimelyinstitutional and clinical intervention

TI Importance of Digital Teacher Competencies (DTC) in Higher Education
SO REVISTA ELECTRONICA CALIDAD EN LA EDUCACION SUPERIOR
LA Spanish
DT Article
DE Teacher competencies; digital competence; education; teaching;
   information technology
AB This research analyzed the importance of digital teaching competencies (DTCs) in higher education, emphasizing their transformative role in the face of technological evolution. The study emphasizes the importance of integrate technical, pedagogical, and attitudinal skills to create meaningful and equitable learning experiences stemming from the digital revolution and ICTs. The study employed a qualitative approach to document analysis using national and international databases, prioritizing frameworks such as UNESCO (2019) and DigCompEdu to describe the evolution and challenges. Additionally, the study explores the history of ICTs in Costa Rica since 1985, professional teaching competencies, and 21st-century profiles. It also addresses limitations such as scarce policies, resistance to change, and the relationship between DTCs and pedagogical practice. The integrative model proposes a matrix that merges DigCompEdu, UNESCO, and other authors, articulating professional, pedagogical, and student dimensions for a reflective and inclusive transformation. Finally, the study concludes with a call for urgent need for institutional policies, continuous training, and pedagogical evaluation of ICT to bridge digital divides and improve the quality of education.

TI Laboratory practices in contingency contexts: An academic strategy in
   higher education
SO REVISTA ELECTRONICA CALIDAD EN LA EDUCACION SUPERIOR
LA Spanish
DT Article
DE practice; active learning; educational strategy; food processing;
   agro-industrial; education; pandemic; distance learning
AB During the COVID-19 pandemic, the Agroindustrial Engineering program at the Universidad Estatal a Distancia (UNED) implemented an academic strategy to ensure educational continuity and the development of student abilities. In response to health restrictions, the laboratory practices of engineering courses, which are normally conducted in person at an educational pilot plant, were adapted to a home-based format. TI Product design using food waste-derived biomaterials in a COIL
   framework: an intercultural and multidisciplinary experience across
   Mexico, Chile, and Panama
SO REVISTA ELECTRONICA CALIDAD EN LA EDUCACION SUPERIOR
LA Spanish
DT Article
DE COIL; Educational Innovation; Internationalization
ID HIGHER-EDUCATION; INTERNATIONALIZATION
AB This study analyzes the educational impact of an online Collaborative Online International Learning (COIL) experience focused on product design using biomaterials derived from food waste, implemented across higher education institutions in Mexico, Chile, and Panama. It is an empirical study with a quantitative approach, employing a non-experimental, cross-sectional design with a descriptive-exploratory scope. The sample consisted of 11 students from different disciplines, selected through non-probabilistic convenience sampling. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire with Likert-type items, organized into three dimensions: perception of the learning process, development of collaborative and intercultural competencies, and professional projection. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, including frequency distributions and measures of central tendency. The results show a high level of positive evaluation of the experience, with more than 80% of participants reporting favorable outcomes in the development of collaborative and intercultural skills, as well as in the application of knowledge to real-world problems. However, challenges were identified, particularly related to team coordination, asynchronous communication, and trust-building in multicultural virtual environments.<br /> It is concluded that the COIL approach represents an effective strategy for fostering transversal competencies and advancing curriculum internationalization, especially in interdisciplinary contexts oriented toward sustainability. Nevertheless, the findings should be interpreted with caution due to the small sample size and the exploratory nature of the study.
